name: Karelian rune-singing (Kalevala-meter)
lineage: Karelian rune-singing tradition of the Karelian (Karjala) ethno-linguistic region straddling the Finnish-Russian border (eastern Finland, Russian Karelia), comprising the canonical Finno-Karelian narrative-and-magical-incantation oral-poetic corpus from which Elias Lönnrot compiled the Kalevala national-epic (first edition 1835, expanded second edition 1849). Performance: solo or duo unaccompanied voice in strict Kalevala-meter (four-stress eight-syllable trochaic line), often performed antiphonally with one singer providing a low-register drone or echo to the other's melodic line. The Karelian-Finnish runo-singer historical tradition was nearly extinguished by twentieth-century Soviet-and-Finnish modernization; documentary collection by Lönnrot and subsequent collectors preserved approximately 200,000 verses. Distinguished from broader Finnic vocal-music by rune-singing's strict Kalevala-meter and oral-epic-narrative orientation.
